choices.text: 5.1.1, about collecting data and asking for permission

choices.text: 4.2, Minimum Functionality

choices.text: What the app does

choices.text: How many screens it has

prompt: Google Play's spam policy is aimed at which kind of WebView app, by the lesson?

choices.text: One showing a site its developer does not own or run

prompt: Which of these are tells a person notices in a wrapped app, from the lesson's list? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: the back gesture leaves the app from a deeper screen
choices.why: It should go back a screen.

choices.text: text can be selected and the page zoomed
choices.why: Nothing else on the phone allows it.

choices.text: nothing works offline
choices.why: A person opens it on a train.

choices.text: the icon is square
choices.why: Icons are lesson 13, and not a tell.

prompt: A company wraps its marketing site, five pages and a contact form, and submits it to the App Store. What does the lesson suggest the reviewer sees?

choices.text: A normal app, since it was built with real native projects
choices.why: The projects do not change what the app does.

choices.text: Marketing material in a frame, the case 4.2.2 names

choices.text: A security risk
choices.why: Not the issue.

choices.text: A performance problem
choices.why: Five pages are not slow.

prompt: Match each wish to what it takes in a Capacitor app.

a plugin plus accounts and keys with Apple and Google

pairs.left: a reminder at a set time

prompt: Why was lesson 4's reminder scheduled with the system instead of a timer in the page?

choices.text: Timers are not allowed in a WebView
choices.why: They are, while the page runs.

choices.text: The system suspends the app in the background
choices.why: Right. A timer in the page stops with it.

choices.text: The system's timer is more accurate than one in the page
choices.why: Accuracy is not the reason.

choices.text: Apple's rule 4.2 requires it
choices.why: No.

prompt: A planner feature counts a study session's minutes with the screen off, in a setInterval. What does the lesson say happens on a phone?

choices.why: Both systems suspend it.

choices.why: The design fails before any review.

choices.text: It stops; the time is worked out when the app opens again
choices.why: Right. The design has to be rebuilt around the system's limits.

prompt: What does the lesson call the middle road between a pure wrapper and a native rewrite?

choices.text: Web screens in a native shell, with a few native parts

choices.text: A Progressive Web App, installed from the browser instead of a store
choices.why: That is no store at all.

choices.text: Two apps, one per store
choices.why: No.

choices.text: Cordova
choices.why: Not what the lesson means.

prompt: By how many times did ceiling.mjs slow the processor in its first three runs?
Why does ceiling.mjs measure the site npm run preview serves, rather than npm run dev?

choices.text: Preview runs on a phone
choices.why: It runs on the computer.

choices.text: The dev server cannot be slowed
choices.why: The browser is slowed, not the server.

choices.text: The dev server adds work of its own

choices.text: Playwright cannot open port 5173 when the processor is slowed
choices.why: It can.

prompt: A tap takes about a second at five thousand sessions. What did the lesson conclude about whose ceiling that is?

choices.text: Chromium's, since phones use another engine
choices.why: Android's WebView is Chromium.

choices.text: Playwright's measuring overhead
choices.why: It is small beside a second.
